No single node disconnects the graph, but removing D and E together does, so the cohesion (node connectivity) is 2. The card shows the cut D, E and the value 2." width="100%"} The cohesion is the minimum number of nodes whose removal would disconnect the graph. Also called node connectivity. Only defined for undirected graphs. Returns `0` if already disconnected. This is an alias for `get_node_connectivity()` that additionally rejects directed graphs. Cohesion summarizes how robust a network is to node failures: a graph with cohesion `k` stays connected after any `k - 1` nodes are removed. For a connected graph with at least three nodes, a cohesion of `1` means it has an articulation point (see `get_articulation_points()`), and a cohesion of `2` or more means it is biconnected. Cohesion is never larger than adhesion (see `get_adhesion()`), which in turn is never larger than the minimum node degree. A complete graph `K_n` has cohesion `n - 1`. Graphs with fewer than two nodes, or that are already disconnected, return `0`. Use `get_node_connectivity_between()` for a specific pair of nodes. The method does not modify the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum node cut size: the smallest number of nodes whose removal disconnects the graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A 4-cycle stays connected after removing any one node, but removing two opposite nodes disconnects it, so its cohesion is 2: ::: {#23eafcd8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")]) ) graph.get_cohesion() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Cohesion can be lower than adhesion. Two triangles that share a single node `C` need two edge removals to disconnect, but removing node `C` alone splits them: ::: {#ddc8179c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} bowtie = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "C")]) ) bowtie.get_cohesion(), bowtie.get_adhesion() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (1, 2) ``` ::: :::
